mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across monetary policy cycles.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is observed, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings declines and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5, or the Rank IC for UNRATE > 4.5 is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (INDPRO falling below 100), production constraints lead to higher input costs and reduced corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC for INDPRO < 100 is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 1300, or the Rank IC for HOUST < 1300 is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS > 4.5 is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 159000 thousand units signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS < 159000, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS < 159000 is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy response to high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
